//: The EDITOR project (app.imagehorse.app). Read only when the Vercel project's
Root Directory is set to `app` — that setting is what makes Vercel pick up this
file instead of the repo-root vercel.json, which belongs to the marketing site.
Two projects cannot share one config file, so the split is by root directory.
⚠️ NOT YET VALIDATED BY A REAL DEPLOY. This is a port of the working command in
netlify.toml, and every pin in it is load-bearing — read that file's comments
before touching the build command. netlify.toml is deliberately still in the
repo and still live; retire it only once a deploy from here has been checked
Two Vercel project settings have no equivalent here and must be set in the
dashboard: Root Directory = app, and 'Include files outside of the Root
Directory' = ON. The second is required — the Rust crate, Cargo.toml,
rust-toolchain.toml and scripts/ all live above app/.
installCommand: echo 'install is part of buildCommand — the wasm engine has to exist before pnpm build'
//buildCommand: Lifted from netlify.toml, which is the source of truth for this chain. The
two pins matter for the same reasons documented there: --default-toolchain none
leaves rust-toolchain.toml as the only thing choosing a compiler, and the
wasm-pack version pin keeps wasm-opt's output a function of the repo. Do not
The trailing move exists because Vercel's outputDirectory is resolved inside
the root directory and app/vite.config.ts writes to ../www-dist, which is
outside it. Building to www-dist and then moving keeps Netlify's publish path
working byte-for-byte while it is still live, instead of changing the Vite
output and breaking the deploy that is currently serving users.
buildCommand: cd .. && curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none && source $HOME/.cargo/env && cargo install wasm-pack --version 0.15.0 --locked && ./scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm install && pnpm --filter stamp-tool build && ./scripts/write-build-info.sh www-dist && rm -rf app/dist && mv www-dist app/dist
//rewrites: The editor IS a single-page app, so unlike the marketing site it keeps its
catch-all: every in-app route is served by the one index.html. There is no
prerendering here and none is wanted — the app is behind a canvas, there is
nothing for a crawler to read, and the SEO argument lives on imagehorse.app.

headers.//: Content-hashed by Vite, so a changed file is a changed URL.
